subject: Certification readiness pulse: ISO 27001 & FedRAMP sequencing
messages:
From: Kate Holloway <kate.holloway@greenbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@greenbank.com>
Date: 2027-03-28 09:12 -0700
Subject: Certification readiness pulse: ISO 27001 & FedRAMP sequencing

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we prepare our internal procurement checklist, legal and InfoSec are asking for a concise sequencing plan: GreenBank needs to understand whether pursuing ISO 27001 first (and then FedRAMP tailoring) or running both in parallel is more realistic for Redwood given your current evidence posture.

Quick asks from our side so we can align stakeholders tomorrow:
- Can you confirm current ISO scope (services in-scope) and any major gaps vs. ISO 27001 control families?
- Do you have an estimated timeline (months) for a minimal set of remediation activities to hit a pre-audit posture?
- For FedRAMP, are there dependencies on your private (VPC/on-prem) offering that would extend timelines?

We also need a list of sample artifacts for the next 30-day evidence window (logs, config snapshots, SSAE traces). If you can attach the latest intake index that would be ideal.

Thanks — attaching our internal intake template (for your visibility).

Best,
Kate
Security Program Manager
GreenBank
[Attachment: GB-intake-template.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Holloway <kate.holloway@greenbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Certification readiness pulse: ISO 27001 & FedRAMP sequencing

Kate — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, followed by a short plan and our attachments:

Short answers:
- ISO scope: currently covers the hosted API surface (text generation, embeddings) and the control plane; Dedicated and Private options are in-scope for controls related to data handling but a final boundary doc is in draft (see attached ISO-scope-diagram.png).
- Timeline to pre-audit posture: with current velocity and assuming we dedicate an evidence sprint, we estimate 3–4 months to close high-priority gaps (access reviews, logging completeness, control narratives).
- FedRAMP dependencies: the primary extension is documentation around VPC/private deployments (network diagrams, SSP addenda). That typically adds 6–9 weeks of packaging work beyond ISO work, not accounting for auditor scheduling.

Requested artifacts (we've attached an initial index):
- evidence_index.csv (covers log retention, IAM roles, KMS key manifests, backup snapshots)
- SIG_v2.xlsx (our updated SIG answers; flagged items with "ACTION_REQUIRED")
- ISO-scope-diagram.png (draft scope diagram)

Proposed sequencing (high level):
1) Immediate (weeks 0–4): evidence sprint to gather snapshots for 30-day window, assign control owners, produce control narratives for high-risk controls.
2) Near term (weeks 5–12): close identified gaps (access reviews, logging adjustments), freeze scope, tabletop with auditors for sample windows.
3) Parallel packaging (weeks 6–16): begin FedRAMP SSP addenda where Private/Dedicated specifics are needed. This runs in parallel but depends on finalized scope.

Can we book a 30-minute checkpoint tomorrow at 11am PT to agree owners and a concrete artifact list? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and add a short mutual action plan.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SIG_v2.xlsx (xlsx); Attachment: evidence_index.csv (csv); Attachment: ISO-scope-diagram.png (png)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Holloway <kate.holloway@greenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28 11:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Certification readiness pulse: ISO 27001 & FedRAMP sequencing

Kate — adding a couple of operational specifics so expectations are clear:

Operational notes:
- Evidence collection: we can provide 30/60/90-day log snapshots and IAM audit reports. For FedRAMP, auditors will want network capture and longer retention proof for boundary-enforced deployments.
- Remediation velocity: if GreenBank can confirm the list of priority controls (e.g., encryption-at-rest, privileged access reviews) we’ll prioritize engineering tickets and aim for a two-week sprint cadence for critical patches.
- Auditors & windows: we recommend scheduling the pre-assessment after the 3–4 month sprint — auditors typically want 30 days of stable evidence post-remediation.

Scheduling: 11am PT works for me. Also propose a short pre-read: I’ll upload a 1-page MOP (method of procedure) that shows artifact pull steps for Teams/Infra.

Ben Carter
Security Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MOP-evidence-pull.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kate Holloway <kate.holloway@greenbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@greenbank.com>
Date: 2027-03-28 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Certification readiness pulse: ISO 27001 & FedRAMP sequencing

Thanks, Marissa and Ben — that level of detail helps a lot. We’ll: 
- Confirm our priority controls and share by end of day (Tom will own)
- Accept the 11am PT checkpoint (please send invite)
- Expect the evidence_index.csv and SIG_v2.xlsx as the working artifacts for our compliance team review

One question for tomorrow: do you have a standard confidentiality addendum you prefer before we share internal policy docs (some of ours reference third-party provider security profiles)? If so, please attach.

Best,
Kate
Security Program Manager
GreenBank
